description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities . Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the grant award letter, the dates for submission of the annual reports are mentioned. In case of a three-year project, between 5-7 reports are obligatory. The first report (0) is a very short report which focuses on specific conditions and/or recommendations in the grant. There is no need to report on progress in achieving outputs and outcomes, which is done in the first annual report. As annex to the report 0, the consortium agreements between the partners should be submitted. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

actual.value:
Overal 31 people were trained by Dance4Life over the course of the granting period. 24 women and girls and 7 boys and men. Including 4 members of the LGBT community and 1 person from the Roma community.
From 24 Jan – 7 Feb 2022, Dance4Life conducted an online onboarding for some of the key YVNO staff, staff from the network’s member organisations and some of the network’s young volunteers (11 people in total). The point of this onboarding was to introduce Dance4Life’s model and peer-led CSE curriculum to YVNO; to agree on who the peer-facilitators should be and how to recruit them; and create an overall roadmap for the implementation of the Dance4Life model in Albania. For this onboarding, the YVN team went through a series 5 online modules on Dance4Life’s e-learning platform and took part in 7 online meetings with the Dance4Life team. The online modules covered the following topics: the Journey4Life; Champions4Life; Creating an enabling environment; Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning; and Safeguarding young people.
This was followed by a 7-day online contextualisation workshop from 9-21 March 2022 whereby the Dance4Life team assisted 10 members of the YVNO team in adapting Dance4Life’s CSE curriculum – the Journey4Life – to the SRHR needs of young people in Albania. YVNO conducted a thorough desk review of the SRHR issues affecting young people in Albania and tailored the activities and the language of the Journey4Life to their local context.
Finally, from 6-12 May 2022, YVNO and Rutgers facilitated a 7-day training in Durrës, Albania, and successfully trained 20 young Albanians aged 17-26 years old to become peer facilitators – or Champions4Life as we call them. These peer-facilitators were trained to deliver a contextualised version of the Journey4Life to young people in different high schools and universities across Albania.
Participants filled in post-training evaluations following the YVNO onboarding and the peer-facilitator training. The YVNO team gave the onboarding training a rating of 9.25/10. All participants agreed that the training objectives had been met and that they now felt capacitated to implement the Journey4Life in Albania.
Following the peer-facilitator training: all trainees said they understood young people’s rights to SRHR information and services and felt confident to empower young people to make a change; 95% of trainees felt confident that they could deliver the SRHR content from the Journey4Life and refer young people to the right SRH services; 70% of participants felt ‘super confident’ to deliver the Journey4Life to groups of young people in their community, and the remaining 30% said they ‘know the principles of delivery well and think they can do it’.
Unfortunately, pre-training evaluations were not carried out before either training.
After the Champion4Life training, YVNO organised 3 follow-up meetings with the Champions4Life to agree on follow-up activities. Starting in September 2022, the 20 Champions4Life will deliver 12 Journey4Life encounters in pairs in 4 different regions of Albania (10 pairs \* 12 encounters \* 20 young partcipants).
In addition, the Champions4Life are involved in other youth SRH programs implemented by YVNO and UNFPA Y-PEER Program. They are engaged as Peer Educators and provide different youth peer education sessions.
Champions4Life are also involved in creating an enabling environment for SRHR in Albania by taking part in various stakeholder meetings. For example, the Champions met the Dutch ambassador to Albania at the Embassy of the Netherlands in Albania, they participated in a meeting with staff from the French Embassy in Albania, they met with the UNFPA Team, and joined meetings with other NGOs and members of YVNO. During these meetings, Champions4Life demonstrated some of the activities of the Journey4Life and raised awareness about young people’s SRHR needs in Albania. These events showed that young people are ready to practice the skills and knowledge they have acquired from the training.
As part of the meetings with stakeholders, YVNO and representatives from Dance4Life held a meeting with the Minister of Youth and Children. After the meeting, a desk review of the current situation was shared with the Minister. This meeting served to create bridges of cooperation that were not there earlier and make the Ministry of Youth and Children aware of the importance of achieving sexual and reproductive health rights.
As part of this project, Dance4Life’s Journey4Life curriculum was adapted to the Albanian context and translated into the Albanian language. Following the peer-facilitator training, the document is currently being further improved, taking into account trainees’ feedback. It will them be printed and each peer-facilitator will be given a copy. This manual provides them with everything they need to successfully deliver Journey4Life sessions to young people in Albania.
In addition, YVNO partnered with the German Federal Center for Health Education (BZgA) to translate and print 2 International ASRH documents:
-Standards for Sexuality Education:[https://www.bzga-whocc.de/en/publications/standards-for-sexuality-education/](https://www.bzga-whocc.de/en/publications/standards-for-sexuality-education/)
-Guidance for Implementation of the Standards: [https://www.bzga-whocc.de/en/publications/guidance-for-implementation-of-the-standards/](https://www.bzga-whocc.de/en/publications/guidance-for-implementation-of-the-standards/)
Both documents have been translated in Albanian and printed 1000 times each. YVNO is distributing these documents to its member organisations and to the Ministry of Education, Sports and Youth, which is responsible for providing Comprehensive Sexual Education. Thanks to the UNFPA Country Office in Albania, 300 copies of each document are also distributed in North Macedonia, Serbia and Kosovo. This will help these countries to improve the provision of Comprehensive Sexual Education in the region. The documents will be presented to local actors and especially to representatives from the Ministry of Education, Sports and Youth, responsible for providing comprehensive sexual education in educational settings.
